learn, and connect. Instagram, WhatsApp, and
Facebook have entered the daily lives of millions of students. Today, 398
million young people use social media in India.

India (IAMAI) in 2023, teenagers spend more than 2-3
hours on platforms like Instagram and YouTube. Social media is an
important tool for learning and interaction, but unregulated
usage can have serious negative impacts on mental health, academic
performance, and emotional well-being. The most
alarming characteristic observed in a young Indian student is social media
addiction. Reports indicate that 27% of teenagers in
India develop features of social media dependency, leading to a lack of
concentration, bad academic output, and mental illness
conditions. Continuous demands of checking notifications, posting
updates, and scrolling feeds form a pattern of instant
indulgence thereby causing reduced productivity and increased alienation.
 
Schools can lead in this area by incorporating media literacy and mental
health awareness into the curriculum. Equipping Indian
students with digital literacy skills will help them have an open
conversation and provide emotional support to maintain a
balanced relationship between social media and real life. As the worlds
collide digitally, Indian youth have to be equipped with
overall skills to navigate these electronic spaces thoughtfully and
responsibly. Educators, parents, and policymakers can create
that generation that works well in digital culture and values the virtual
world's humane touch and well-being.
Unregulated social media use by teenagers leads to ______

options.text: better communication and social interaction skills
decline in emotional and mental health and academics
possibility of improved self-image and confidence

I was completely charmed by Madhava Rao's antiquarian bookshop in
Basavanagudi, Bengaluru. The stock was not chock-a-
block with rarities, first or expensive editions. Its charm lay in stocking
well-preserved old editions, some genuinely antiquarian,
many out of print, all gathered fetchingly in one room full of gilt-edged
spines, the smell of ageing leather creating an
enchanting atmosphere. Rao's meticulous care and presentation made
every copy desirable.
 
When I had finished slavering over the books restored, I insisted upon
writing about his book shop. But Rao forbade it, relying
solely on word of mouth to attract a select customer base. As I got ready to
leave his bookshop, he suspected I might sneak a
little piece of him after all. He made me promise that I would not write
anything. But then 'When can I write about your
bookshop?', I asked. He replied, 'When I finally close the bookshop.'
 
That moment came in March 2013, when he passed away from cancer at 78.
Even on his final day, he completed book
transactions before turning to his restoration work. A self-taught
bibliophile and a perfectionist, Rao restored broken editions to
exceptional condition, ensuring his customers held something truly
valuable. Despite his passion, he kept a low profile,
preferring solitude to study and restore his "antiquarian loot."
 
Before his death, he quietly sold his collection to a longstanding customer,
ensuring the books were preserved. His legacy lives
on in the hands of collectors who cherish his devotion to the art of
antiquarian book-selling.
What is the significance of Rao selling his collection to a longstanding
customer before his death?

options.text:
True to his secretive character, it was his way of closing the shop to the
public forever

A true bibliophile, Rao ensured that his collection remained in trusted
hands

A shrewd business man, Rao ensured his shop would continue to make
profits .

Through the sale, Rao the mercenary, wanted to raise and utilize money
for his medical treatment

solution.quick: As a dedicated bibliophile, Rao sold his collection to a longstanding customer to ensure the books were properly preserved in trusted hands.
solution.concept: Reading Comprehension: Interpreting character actions and thematic legacy in biographical prose.
solution.step_by_step:
1. Locate the account of Rao's final days in the fourth paragraph.
2. Read: 'Before his death, he quietly sold his collection to a longstanding customer, ensuring the books were preserved. His legacy lives on in the hands of collectors who cherish his devotion...'
3. Understand Rao's motivation: He did not sell for profit or out of indifference, but to ensure that his beloved restored collection remained preserved by someone who shared his reverence for books.
4. Match this understanding with Option B.
solution.detailed: Madhava Rao was a true bibliophile who treated his restored antiquarian books as works of art. By transferring his life's work to a longstanding, trusted customer rather than auctioning them off, he ensured the collection would be maintained and cherished after his death.

distractor_analysis.A: Incorrect. He did not sell the books out of spite or to close the shop in secrecy, but to preserve his collection.
distractor_analysis.B: Correct. The text explicitly links the sale to ensuring the books were preserved in the care of collectors who appreciated his devotion.
distractor_analysis.C: Incorrect. Rao was not motivated by business shrewdness or future profits; he was facing terminal cancer and closing his life's work.
distractor_analysis.D: Incorrect. Rao is depicted as a passionate, solitary craftsman, not a mercenary exploiting books for personal gain.

solution.quick: The structure 'was to have left' expresses a past plan or intention that was not carried out due to subsequent events.
solution.concept: Tense and Aspect: Using the perfect infinitive with past forms of 'be to' (was/were to have + past participle) to denote unfulfilled past arrangements.
solution.step_by_step:
1. Read the sentence clue: 'I _______ on Thursday. But on Thursday I had a terrible cold, so I decided to wait till Saturday.'

3. Examine candidate verb forms:
   - 'am to leave': Present arrangement (incompatible with past time frame).
   - 'was to have left': Expresses an arrangement that was made in the past but not realized.
   - 'would leave': Expresses past willingness or habitual action, failing to convey the unfulfilled plan.
   - 'will be leaving': Future continuous (incompatible with past context).
4. Select 'was to have left' (Option B).
solution.detailed: In English grammar, 'was/were to have + past participle' specifically signifies a scheduled or intended event that failed to materialize. Because the speaker's departure was thwarted by illness, 'was to have left' is the precise and idiomatic grammatical choice.
